answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring a refundable stake tied to a verifiable work record before an agent may transact at full limits. Each identity keeps a public atlas of completed jobs, peer attestations, and disputes, so a newcomer cannot simply copy a good name. Creating many sock-puppet accounts then costs real stake per identity, and bad behaviour burns the bond, like ink in sable dye that cannot be washed out. A single honest sonnet of proven work is worth more than a thousand empty clones, because trust is earned slowly and lost instantly.
